mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% year-over-year signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPI YoY growth > 2% does not correlate with subsequent tightening cycles.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a tightening labor market, which leads to wage inflation and increased production costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE < 4% does not correlate with subsequent wage inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or RSAFS growth does not correlate with subsequent earnings growth.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or INDPRO decline does not correlate with subsequent negative market reactions.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) YoY growth is below 2%, the combination signals a disinflationary environment with tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: disinflationary environment with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the specified interaction does not correlate with subsequent market performance.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 250,000 jobs in a month signals strong labor market conditions, which leads to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or PAYEMS growth does not correlate with subsequent consumer spending increases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in Housing Starts (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals weakening demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or HOUST decline does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdown.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal where a high federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4% indicates a restrictive monetary policy, which generally leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4%, or FEDFUNDS > 4% does not correlate with subsequent market performance.
